functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans produce thrust; in: fuel at inlet pressure, throttle command (§5.1.4); out: thrust. Independent per engine — continue after loss of any one engine at/after V1 (§5.1.3).
functions.funcDef: Generate and control thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1: 'provide thrust for all phases of flight').

functions.subDef: Two inboard engines provide reverse thrust; in: reverse command, WOW+RA agreement (§5.1.2); out: deceleration. Inhibited in flight; separable from forward-thrust generation (§5.1.2).
functions.funcDef: Generate and control thrust for all phases of flight (SDD §5.1.1).
functions.subName: Provide reverse thrust on the ground

functions.subDef: Trimmable stabiliser with elevators; in: inceptor/autopilot command, air+inertial data (§5.3.4); out: pitch moment. Elevators on HYD A and C; mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim (§5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers; in: inceptor/autopilot command (§5.3.4); out: roll moment. Ailerons on HYD B and C (§5.3.2).
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Split rudder in upper and lower segments, each with own actuation and hydraulic supply (upper←A, lower←B); sizes to outboard-engine-out at V1 with max blade (§5.3.2/§5.3.3). Segments fail independently; lower has mechanical reversion.
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Double-slotted Fowler flaps (four sections) and full-span slats via two independent PDUs through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (§5.3.2); out: high-lift position to performance computation.
functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope (SDD §5.3.1).

functions.subDef: Nose unit and six main bogies (20 tyres); flotation sized for semi-prepared strip (§5.6.2); in: HYD A retraction/extension with free-fall alternate (§5.6.2); out: gear position, WOW.
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, absorb loads, spread footprint pressure, and provide braking and directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support and roll on the surface
functions.funcName: Support the aircraft on the ground and decelerate

functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc, normal from HYD B, alternate HYD A, accumulator-supported emergency (§5.6.2); anti-skid per wheel pair; sizing case 1,800 m vs ~1,080 m rollout (§5.6.3). Independent of extension path.
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, provide braking and directional control (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.funcName: Support the aircraft on the ground and decelerate

functions.subDef: Hydraulic steering from tillers and rudder pedals with mechanical disconnect for towing (§5.6.2); independent capability from braking (separate harnesses §5.6.5).
functions.funcDef: Provide directional control on the ground (SDD §5.6.1).
functions.funcName: Support the aircraft on the ground and decelerate

functions.subDef: Upward-hinging visor driven by HYD A with electric backup (§5.7.2); in: crew/ground command; out: door position. Cannot operate in flight (§5.7.6).
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in access to the full hold length via the nose visor and form the pressure boundary when closed (SDD §5.7.1). Structural load path excluded — treated as structure per §5.7.3.
functions.subName: Open and close the nose visor

functions.subDef: Twelve latches on common torque shaft, eight independent pins on a separate supply; dual dissimilar lock sensing; pressure interlock <0.1 psi (§5.7.2); out: lock status to take-off config monitor. Independent of visor drive.
functions.funcDef: Secure the nose visor and confirm lock integrity (SDD §5.7).

functions.subDef: Nine saddles, two tension straps each, electric winches locked mechanically; loss of one strap carried by neighbours (§5.8.3); in: WOW, loading plan; out: strap tension to flight deck. Lateral/vertical restraint by saddle geometry.
functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade up to 72.6 t along the full hold length through all flight and ground load cases (SDD §5.8.1). Hold floor hard points excluded — no redundancy, treated as structure (§5.8.3).

functions.subDef: Single instrumented tension loop over every strap; annunciates loss on any strap, and two adjacent stations as a restraint condition (§5.8.2). Coverage is a recorded single-run item (§5.8.3).
functions.funcDef: Monitor restraint integrity in flight (SDD §5.8.2).

functions.subDef: Two air-cycle packs on bleed via cross-bleed manifold, either pack from either side; flight deck and hold separate conditioning zones (§5.9.2); in: bleed, ram air; out: conditioned air.
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold, and control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).

functions.subDef: Two digital controllers driving two outflow valves (either sufficient), pneumatic backup, independent mechanical relief (§5.9.2); out: differential/cabin altitude to avionics, oxygen logic, nose-door interlock. Independent of air conditioning.
functions.funcDef: Control fuselage pressure differential (SDD §5.9.1).

functions.subDef: Wing leading edges and engine cowls by hot bleed (piccolo); stabiliser leading edges electrically heated in six independent zones (§5.10.2); out: zone health to avionics. Bleed and electric zones fail independently.
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion is unacceptable, for the icing envelope of the cert basis (SDD §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect airframe surfaces and inlets from ice

functions.subDef: Probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors electrically heated and monitored individually; two detectors of same type on opposite sides (§5.10.2); out: ice detection advisory. Commonality of detector type recorded (§5.10.3).
functions.funcDef: Protect probes and detect icing (SDD §5.10.1).

functions.subDef: Four display units and two HUDs on three display processors over dual networks; three ADIRUs; independent standby instrument sharing no supply/sensor/processing (§5.11.2); out: displays to crew.
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Present flight, navigation and system information

functions.subDef: Alerting consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures, on two independent processing channels (§5.11.2); out: alerts to crew. Independent of display presentation.
functions.funcDef: Consolidate and prioritise crew alerting (SDD §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Alert the crew to failures and procedures

functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU (AND logic, degrading to single-loop); bleed-duct and gear-bay overheat; hold smoke detection at nine stations (§5.12.2); out: warnings to alerting.
functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress (SDD §5.12.1).

functions.subDef: Two bottles per engine pair, cross-plumbed to either nacelle; single dedicated APU bottle auto-discharged unattended (§5.12.2); in: fire handle command, hot battery bus power; out: discharge status. Hold has no suppression (§5.12.2).
functions.funcDef: Extinguish or suppress detected fire (SDD §5.12.1).

functions.subDef: Two HP cylinders on a common manifold with crossover feeding four quick-donning demand-regulated masks; either cylinder capable at reduced reserve (§5.13.2/§5.13.3); in: crew donning; out: oxygen to four stations. No passenger oxygen — hold unoccupied.
functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and the following descent/diversion (SDD §5.13.1).

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change without crew command (malfunction of forward thrust generation)
fha.effAc: Thrust departs from the commanded value with no crew command; net trajectory effect (speed/energy and, if one engine, yaw) depends on magnitude and direction, which the function definition does not bound.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the departure and re-establish the intended thrust; workload increase not bounded by available inputs.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Magnitude and direction of the uncommanded thrust change are not bounded by the function definition or the SDD, so a single aircraft-level effect cannot be derived; needs a handling-qualities/performance judgement to bound the worst credible excursion before classification.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response to crew command (malfunction of forward thrust generation)
fha.effAc: Thrust delivered differs from that commanded by the crew; resulting energy/trajectory error depends on the size of the discrepancy, which is not bounded by the function definition.
fha.effCrew: Crew command does not produce the expected response; crew must recognise the discrepancy and compensate.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The error magnitude between commanded and delivered thrust is not bounded by the provided function definition or SDD, so the aircraft effect cannot be derived and no class can be committed; requires bounding of the worst credible command error.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slowly developing thrust asymmetry below crew detection threshold (crew-unaware malfunction of forward thrust generation)
fha.effAc: Asymmetry accumulates without crew awareness; trim/autopilot may mask it until control authority or trim range is approached, at which point recovery margin is reduced. Trim and autopilot authority against a slow asymmetry are not defined in the provided inputs.
fha.effCrew: Per the FCIM this is the crew-unaware case: crew continue normal duties and take no action; the condition is not annunciated below the detection threshold.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect depends on remaining trim/autopilot authority when the masked asymmetry is finally revealed, which is not defined in the function definition or SDD; without that bound the worst-case effect cannot be derived and no class can be committed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of forward thrust generation (reduced thrust available from one or more engines)
fha.effAc: Reduced total thrust; asymmetry if confined to one side. The aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine at or after V1, with rudder authority sized to the outboard-engine-out case. A partial loss short of full engine-out reduces climb performance and increases directional trim demand.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage thrust asymmetry through rudder/trim and follow engine-out procedures; increased workload during take-off/climb.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects support a significant reduction in functional capability / significant increase in crew workload short of the full engine-out design case, which the aircraft is explicitly designed to survive to a suitable aerodrome. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of forward thrust generation (all four engines)
fha.effAc: Total loss of propulsive thrust; the aircraft cannot maintain level flight and is committed to a forced landing. No thrust source remains.
fha.effCrew: Crew face an unpowered forced landing with minimal options; extreme workload and reduced probability of a survivable outcome.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of all forward thrust prevents continued flight and normally results in loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment in flight
fha.effAc: Uncommanded reverse thrust in flight produces a large asymmetric thrust and drag transient on the affected inboard engine, degrading directional control and lift, with potential loss of control depending on phase and speed. Deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock; this condition assumes defeat of those interlocks.
fha.effCrew: Sudden asymmetry and yaw/roll upset demanding immediate corrective action; high probability of exceeding controllability under some conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded in-flight reverse thrust is a large-transient asymmetry that can result in loss of control and loss of the airplane; proposed Catastrophic pending confirmation of controllability at the inboard reverser moment arm across the envelope. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric reverse thrust on the ground (reverse commanded/deployed on one inboard engine only)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD confirms reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only and are cross-inhibited in flight, but it does not state the ground directional-control margin, steering/braking compensation, or overrun consequence of a single-side ground reverser asymmetry on the 1,800 m semi-prepared surface. Need the ground controllability/stopping-distance effect to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground reverse thrust
fha.effAc: Reduced reverse-thrust deceleration on the ground. Braking is the primary deceleration means with a stated margin between the 1,800 m landing requirement and ~1,080 m predicted rollout; reverse thrust is a supplementary contributor whose loss erodes stopping margin, particularly on the semi-prepared surface.
fha.effCrew: Crew rely more heavily on wheel braking and available runway; increased attention during rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD gives the landing-distance requirement and predicted rollout but does not quantify the reverse-thrust contribution to stopping distance, so the residual margin (and hence overrun risk) with reverse thrust partially lost is not derivable. Need the reverse-thrust credit in the landing-performance case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground reverse thrust
fha.effAc: Reverse thrust (inboard engines only) unavailable; ground deceleration relies on wheel braking and aerodynamic drag against the stated landing margin.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the aircraft effect depends on the wheel-braking degradation case and the residual stopping margin on a semi-prepared surface (rollout vs requirement), which is not established by this function. Reverse thrust is a supplement, not the primary stopping means. Requires the combined braking+reverse stopping analysis before an aircraft effect and severity can be stated.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches other than as commanded; potential departure from the intended flight path and, at critical phases, from controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the erroneous response and counter it; recovery may be beyond available authority depending on magnitude and phase.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An erroneous pitch response the crew commands against but which produces motion other than intended can, at critical phases and magnitude, cause loss of control / departure from controlled flight leading to loss of the airplane. Classified from the stated aircraft effect, subject to engineering confirmation of the achievable erroneous magnitude and phase. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no command
fha.effAc: Aircraft pitches with no crew command; uncommanded trajectory change that, at critical phases and magnitude, can cause departure from controlled flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise an uncommanded excursion and arrest it; time available is phase-dependent and may be insufficient at low altitude.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded pitch excursion perceptible to the crew can, at low altitude or high magnitude, exceed available recovery margin and lead to loss of the airplane. Classified from the stated aircraft effect; confirm achievable magnitude, rate and phase against recovery capability. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Slowly developing erroneous pitch response below crew detection threshold
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue normal duties and take no corrective action while the deviation develops.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware, no-action case: the aircraft outcome depends on whether a slow sub-threshold pitch deviation trends into a significant flight-path or trim excursion before it becomes detectable, or is bounded by envelope/trim limits. That progression is not established by the function definition, so the aircraft effect cannot be stated and severity cannot be derived. Requires analysis of the deviation trajectory and detection threshold.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch trim runaway below crew detection threshold
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; continue normal duties and take no corrective action while the trim runs away below the detection threshold.
fha.effPax: Flight crew only; no hold occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware, no-action case: the aircraft effect of a slow trim runaway depends on the accumulated out-of-trim condition reached before detection and the resulting mistrim / potential out-of-trim recovery difficulty — not established by the function definition. Cannot state an aircraft effect, so severity is left empty pending trim-runaway progression and recovery analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: partial loss of pitch control authority within MAC limits
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch control authority; aircraft controllable within managed CG envelope with degraded manoeuvre/trim margins.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to manage pitch; degraded law annunciated; crew flies within reduced envelope.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects as stated are a significant reduction in functional capability and a significant increase in crew workload with the aircraft remaining controllable within the CG envelope. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: partial loss of pitch control authority outside MAC limits
fha.effAc: Pitch authority insufficient to trim/control at CG positions outside the managed envelope; large reduction in safety margins; aircraft potentially uncontrollable in pitch at limiting CG.
fha.effCrew: Excessive crew workload; may be unable to maintain the aircraft within the safe flight envelope at limiting CG/loading.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of pitch authority outside MAC limits, with a single high-mass unitised blade payload, is a large reduction in safety margins with excessive workload — driven by the outside-MAC condition, not the within-MAC case. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: complete loss of pitch control
fha.effAc: No means of pitch control by any path; loss of control of aircraft trajectory in pitch.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to control the flight path in pitch by any available means.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of pitch control by any means is loss of the airplane; a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim exists in the design but complete loss of pitch control by definition assumes all means lost. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: erroneous roll response to crew command
fha.effAc: Roll response differs from commanded (wrong magnitude/direction); trajectory departs from intended in roll axis.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the erroneous response; increased workload; recovery depends on phase and altitude available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the SDD does not state the magnitude, authority, or rate of an erroneous roll response, nor whether envelope protection bounds it, so the aircraft-level effect (recoverable upset vs departure from controlled flight, and phase dependence) cannot be derived. Needs FCS erroneous-command authority/rate limits and low-altitude exposure to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: uncommanded roll motion with no command
fha.effAc: Roll motion develops with no crew command; trajectory departs in roll; severity depends on rate/authority and altitude available for recovery.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise and arrest an uncommanded roll; workload and recoverability depend on rate and phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the SDD does not state the authority or rate of an uncommanded roll (e.g. runaway actuator vs bounded hardover) nor the low-altitude/approach exposure, so whether this is a recoverable upset or a departure from controlled flight cannot be derived from the provided material.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of roll control
fha.effAc: Aircraft cannot be controlled about the roll axis by any means; bank angle cannot be arrested or reversed, precluding maintenance of a safe flight path and a survivable landing.
fha.effCrew: No means available to the crew to arrest or command roll; loss of aircraft control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of a primary flight-path control axis with no residual means precludes continued safe flight and landing. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority within MAC limits
fha.effAc: Roll control retained but at reduced authority; aircraft controllable within the manoeuvre/authority limits, with reduced margin to demanded roll rates.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to fly within the reduced authority; degraded law annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect magnitude depends on how much roll authority remains and the margin to the sizing (engine-out with max blade) case; the SDD does not quantify residual authority for a within-limits partial loss, so the aircraft effect cannot be sized. Severity left blank pending that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority outside MAC limits
fha.effAc: Roll authority reduced below that needed to hold intended flight path in demanding conditions; large reduction in manoeuvre/roll-control margin, with difficulty countering upset or crosswind.
fha.effCrew: Excessive workload to maintain the flight path within the residual authority; degraded law annunciated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
