No workload or safety-margin effect can be grounded, so severity is left blank.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous indication of adequate strap tension masking a real restraint loss (misleading tension indication)
fha.effAc: A real restraint loss is masked by an erroneous adequate-tension indication; the underlying restraint condition (up to loss of longitudinal restraint of the blade) develops undetected.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the real loss — misled by the erroneous indication, they take no action; the masking defeats the annunciation the restraint design relies on.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot derive a severity: the effect depends on the severity of the masked underlying restraint loss and how far it progresses undetected, which the SDD does not quantify. This misleading condition should be assessed against the worst masked SF-012 condition once that is classified; severity left blank pending that basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of strap-tension monitoring coverage — tension state at one or more stations no longer instrumented
fha.effAc: A subset of restraint stations is no longer monitored; a developing loss or slackening of restraint at an unmonitored station is not annunciated. With restraint itself intact and neighbouring straps sized to carry a single-strap loss, no immediate aircraft effect; the effect is reduced flight-crew awareness of restraint state.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains indication for the remaining covered stations but has no annunciation for the uncovered stations; increased reliance on pre-flight verification.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is loss of monitoring COVERAGE, not loss of restraint. Aircraft consequence depends on the probability and effect of an undetected restraint failure at an uncovered station coincident with the coverage loss — that combined condition is not defined by the monitoring function alone. Cannot ground an aircraft-level severity without the restraint-loss consequence (blade shift / CG) that the unmonitored station would otherwise annunciate.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of strap-tension monitoring — no station instrumented, no restraint-loss annunciation available
fha.effAc: No station is monitored; any developing loss, slackening or two-adjacent-station restraint condition goes unannunciated in flight. Restraint itself remains intact at dispatch, so no immediate aircraft effect; the aircraft is left with no in-flight indication that a restraint condition is developing.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses the restraint-condition annunciation entirely, including the two-adjacent-station immediate-attention alert; no in-flight means to detect a developing restraint problem.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This is total loss of the MONITORING/annunciation function, not of restraint. The aircraft-level severity turns on the consequence of an undetected restraint failure of a 72.6 t single blade (CG shift / structural / controllability) that the alert would otherwise have caught — that consequence is a property of the restraint and payload functions, not stated for the monitoring function alone. Left empty pending that coupled effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous conditioning of supplied air — air delivered to an occupied compartment at an incorrect / hazardous condition (temperature, contamination or fume)
fha.effAc: Conditioned air delivered to the flight deck at an erroneous condition. If contaminated (smoke/fumes) or at a hazardous temperature, the occupied flight deck environment is degraded, potentially impairing the operating crew.
fha.effCrew: Two-crew flight deck is directly exposed; erroneous conditioning delivering smoke/fumes or extreme temperature can cause physical distress or impaired task performance, mitigated by crew oxygen/smoke masks and pack isolation.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous conditioning delivering contaminated or hazardous air to the occupied flight deck can produce physical distress or excessive workload impairing crew task performance; with the two-crew flight deck directly exposed and crew oxygen/smoke masks the compensating means, effects support the Hazardous class. Proposed for confirmation; if a benign erroneous-condition envelope (temperature-only, within crew tolerance) is substantiated, this reduces. [anchor HAZ-2 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced conditioning on single-source (single-pack) operation
fha.effAc: One conditioning source lost; the surviving pack operates to a reduced conditioning schedule, which the design explicitly permits. Flight deck and hold remain conditioned at reduced capability; no loss of pressurisation control.
fha.effCrew: Crew reconfigures to single-pack operation; conditioning available at a reduced schedule with slight increase in monitoring workload.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-pack operation is a permitted, capability-retained degraded state with a reduced conditioning schedule; effects are a slight reduction in a comfort/environmental margin and slight crew workload — consistent with Minor. Proposed for confirmation. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of conditioning to one occupied zone (flight deck)
fha.effAc: Conditioning to the occupied flight deck zone is lost while the hold zone may remain served (or vice versa). The flight deck environment (temperature/ventilation) degrades over time; pressurisation control is a separate function and not implicated by conditioning loss alone.
fha.effCrew: Operating crew experiences a degrading flight-deck environment; depending on duration and outside conditions this progresses from discomfort toward physical distress and increased workload.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; loss of hold conditioning has no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The flight deck and hold are separate conditioning zones, so single-zone loss is credible; but the aircraft-level severity depends on the RATE and magnitude of flight-deck environmental degradation (temperature excursion, ventilation loss, time to crew distress), which is not quantified in the provided material. Cannot derive a class without that time-to-effect data — left empty rather than guessed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of cabin and hold air conditioning
fha.effAc: No effect on aircraft controllability or structure; conditioned-air supply to flight deck and hold lost.
fha.effCrew: Loss of flight-deck temperature/ventilation conditioning; crew comfort degraded and workload increased over time; pressurisation is a separate function and not directly lost by this condition.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no occupant exposure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a firm class from the SDD alone. The document states the flight deck is a conditioning zone held at conventional cabin altitude but does not quantify flight-deck thermal endurance without conditioning, nor whether pressurisation (a separate ECS function) is retained on total loss of conditioning. Effect is bounded to crew comfort/workload if pressure is unaffected (Minor/Major territory) but the workload magnitude and any hypoxia interaction are not derivable — leaving severity empty pending crew-environment substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous commanded cabin differential
fha.effAc: Structure protected against over/under-pressure independently by mechanical relief valves; an erroneous commanded differential can drive cabin/hold pressure to an incorrect but relief-bounded state.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by differential-pressure/cabin-altitude indication; assumed to select manual mode or crew oxygen and initiate descent; increased workload during diagnosis and reconfiguration.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant exposure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Class not derivable without knowing the achievable erroneous differential relative to the relief-valve set points and the flight-deck cabin-altitude excursion the error can produce before relief acts. SDD confirms independent mechanical relief and crew indication but does not quantify the excursion, so the effect between Minor workload and Hazardous margin reduction cannot be pinned — severity left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded change in cabin pressure with no selection
fha.effAc: Cabin/hold pressure changes without crew selection; structure bounded by independent mechanical relief valves; controllability unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware via cabin-altitude/differential indication and (assumed) rate-of-change cues; assumed to don crew oxygen, revert to manual pressurisation and descend; elevated workload and possible physiological onset before mask donning.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant exposure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aware rapid depressurisation to the flight deck could reduce safety margins, but the class depends on the maximum cabin-altitude reached (a function of the preliminary hold/flight-deck differential) and on crew-oxygen availability and donning time, none of which the SDD quantifies. Cannot derive between Major and Hazardous — severity left empty pending cabin-altitude and OXY-diversion substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow drift of cabin pressure below crew detection threshold
fha.effAc: Cabin/hold pressure drifts slowly with no crew action (unaware); structure remains bounded by independent mechanical relief; no controllability effect.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action; insidious cabin-altitude increase can cause progressive hypoxia degrading crew performance before any alerting or physiological cue prompts response; potential for incapacitation if drift continues undetected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant exposure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — This unaware slow-drift condition is the classic incapacitation risk and could be severe, but the class hinges on the maximum cabin altitude the drift can reach given the low (preliminary) differential and on whether independent cabin-altitude alerting bounds exposure — the SDD does not state a cabin-altitude warning or the endurance to hypoxia. Cannot derive between Major and Catastrophic without that; severity left empty rather than guessed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of cabin pressurisation control
fha.effAc: Loss of all automatic and backup pressurisation control (both controllers, both outflow valves and pneumatic backup); independent mechanical positive/negative relief still protects structure. Aircraft is not a high-altitude machine (max FL260) with a low hold differential; flight-deck cabin altitude control lost.
fha.effCrew: Crew don quick-donning oxygen masks (crew oxygen sized for four for the diversion time at max operating altitude), initiate emergency descent and diversion; significant workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the aircraft-level severity from the provided material: the effect turns on the cabin-altitude excursion rate and achievable emergency-descent profile at FL260 with the low hold differential, and on crew-oxygen adequacy for that descent — none of which is quantified in the SDD (differential is explicitly preliminary). Whether the mask-protected emergency descent keeps this at Major or drives it to Hazardous requires the pressurisation/oxygen exposure analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of airframe/inlet ice protection — loss of protection on one or more surface zones
fha.effAc: Ice accretion permitted on the affected protected zone(s) within the icing envelope; degraded aerodynamic/inlet margins on that zone while other zones remain protected; lost electrical zone is annunciated per SDD.
fha.effCrew: Zone-loss annunciated; crew can select manual operation and may exit or avoid icing conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss on one or more zones with the remainder protected and the loss annunciated is a significant reduction in a safety margin/functional capability with increased crew workload to manage/avoid icing; effects stated do not support Hazardous while other zones remain protected and the crew is alerted. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Reduced environmental pack capacity from bleed anti-ice demand while ice protection is in use
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD documents that wing anti-ice in use imposes a bleed demand that reduces pack capacity and applies a displayed performance penalty, but it does not state an aircraft-, crew- or occupant-level safety effect of that reduced pack capacity; without a stated effect the condition cannot be classified. Need the ECS single-source/reduced-schedule consequence at aircraft level to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of airframe/inlet ice protection
fha.effAc: No protection available on wings, inlets, stabiliser, probes, static ports or windshields; unchecked ice accretion within the icing envelope degrades aerodynamic performance, inlet flow and probe/static integrity across all protected zones simultaneously.
fha.effCrew: System off/unavailable; crew must exit and avoid the icing envelope; substantial workload to detect degradation and manage the escape.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of protection across all zones while in the icing envelope is a large reduction in safety margins/functional capabilities with crew workload to escape icing; classification depends on the icing-envelope exposure and escape assumptions flagged — if continued exposure with progressive accretion is credible the condition trends toward Catastrophic, so the engineer should confirm against the icing-envelope definition. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ice-detection advisory (false or missed)
fha.effAc: False advisory commands ice protection when not required, imposing an unnecessary bleed/electrical penalty; a missed advisory fails to command automatic activation, but protection can still be selected on manually at any time and detection is advisory only.
fha.effCrew: With detection advisory and manual selection available, crew can select ice protection on independently of the advisory; a false advisory adds workload, a missed advisory relies on crew recognising conditions.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous advisory (false or missed) with detection being advisory and manual selection available at any time is a significant increase in crew workload / slight-to-significant reduction in margin because automatic activation is defeated but the protective means remains manually selectable; effects stated do not support Hazardous given the manual override. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of individual probe heating
fha.effAc: With no annunciation, a single unheated probe/port may accrete ice in icing conditions and feed erroneous air data into the sensing chain; the SDD states probes are heated AND monitored individually, so an undetected heating loss defeats the monitoring premise. Consequent air-data error can propagate to displays and protections.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally taking no action (unaware case); may act on erroneous air data before any downstream disagreement is detected.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground the aircraft-level outcome from the function definition alone: the SDD says probes/ports/windshields are heated and monitored individually but does not state the consequence of a single undetected element loss on air-data integrity (voting/redundancy across sources, cross-monitoring, and whether one bad source is outvoted). Severity turns on that missing air-data architecture consequence; abstaining rather than guessing.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Misleading flight, navigation or system information presented and undetected by the crew
fha.effAc: Undetected erroneous attitude/airspeed/altitude/navigation drives the crew to fly the aircraft outside the intended flight path or envelope; with no crew detection there is no reversion to standby, potentially leading to loss of control or controlled flight into terrain.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on false information believing it valid; no cue prompts cross-check or reversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected misleading primary flight information with no crew cue to cross-check or revert can lead to loss of control / CFIT — multiple fatalities / loss of the airplane. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight, navigation and system information display
fha.effAc: Primary presentation of flight, navigation and system information is lost; an independent standby instrument sharing no supply, sensor or processing remains available, providing degraded attitude, airspeed and altitude for continued flight and landing.
fha.effCrew: Crew revert to the standby instrument; large increase in workload flying and navigating on standby means, degraded situational awareness particularly in IMC and approach.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of all primary display with only an independent standby retained is a large reduction in functional capability and safety margins with excessive crew workload — but flight remains survivable on the standby means. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of primary display presentation with standby instrument retained
fha.effAc: Partial loss of primary display presentation; the independent standby instrument and remaining display capability provide continued flight, navigation and system information at reduced capability.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload managing reversionary display selection and cross-checking; degraded but adequate information available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss of primary presentation with standby retained is a significant reduction in functional capability and significant increase in crew workload, short of a large reduction in safety margins. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one or more display formats or reference sources
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground an aircraft effect: the function definition does not identify WHICH formats or reference sources are lost, nor what redundancy (three display processors, three reference units, dual networks) remains available in the specific case. Which formats/sources and the residual capability are needed before an effect can be stated and a severity derived.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Spurious or nuisance alerting presented to the crew
fha.effAc: False or nuisance alerts presented against a healthy aircraft state; repeated or high-priority spurious alerting distracts the crew and may cause them to disregard or mistrust a subsequent genuine alert.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in workload managing and discriminating false alerts; risk of desensitisation to valid alerting.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Spurious alerting against a healthy aircraft is a significant increase in crew workload and a distraction, but does not of itself reduce safety margins; effects support Major, not Hazardous. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew alerting and associated procedures — no failure or condition on the aircraft is annunciated and no associated procedure is presented
fha.effAc: Aircraft continues to fly but the crew has no consolidated indication of any system failure or condition; a subsequent or existing failure elsewhere is not annunciated and its procedure is unavailable, so latent failures accumulate undetected and the crew cannot manage them in a timely manner.
fha.effCrew: Crew must self-monitor every system from raw indications without prioritised alerting or procedures; workload rises significantly and detection of a developing failure is delayed or missed.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of alerting removes the crew's primary means of detecting and managing failures; combined with an unannounced further failure this is a large reduction in functional capability and excessive crew workload. Proposed Hazardous for confirmation — Catastrophic is not supported by the function definition alone unless a specific coincident undetected failure sequence is demonstrated. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate an existing failure condition (missed alert) — a genuine failure exists on the aircraft but no alert or procedure is presented for it
fha.effAc: An actual failure condition remains undetected because it is not annunciated; the crew continues normally believing the aircraft is healthy, the mitigating procedure is never actioned, and the underlying condition can progress or combine with a further failure unmitigated.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the existing failure and take no action regarding it; no workload change until the condition manifests through other cues, at which point recovery time is reduced.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A missed alert defeats the mitigation assumed for the underlying failure and can allow an otherwise-managed condition to become unmanaged; large reduction in safety margin proposed as Hazardous for confirmation. The precise class depends on the severity of the specific failures whose annunciation is lost — settle against the alerted conditions in the SFHA. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Incorrect or misleading procedure presented for the condition — an alert is raised but the associated procedure directs the crew to inappropriate action
fha.effAc: The correct failure is annunciated but the presented procedure is wrong or misleading; crew action taken per the erroneous procedure may worsen the condition or disable a serviceable function, degrading safety margins beyond the original failure.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on misleading guidance in good faith; increased workload and potential for an inappropriate configuration change, with delayed recovery once the error is recognised.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on which procedure is misleading and what inappropriate crew action it induces; the function definition alone does not bound the resulting aircraft effect. Cannot classify without identifying the specific procedures affected and their consequence — left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one alerting processing channel — one of two independent processing channels lost, alerting retained on the remaining channel
fha.effAc: Alerting and procedures remain available on the surviving channel; redundancy is reduced to a single channel but the function continues to be performed, with a latent exposure to loss of the second channel.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain full alerting; loss annunciated and dispatch/continued-flight considerations apply. Slight increase in monitoring awareness only.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Function fully retained on the remaining independent channel with reduced redundancy; slight reduction in safety margin proposed as Minor for confirmation, per the dual independent processing-channel architecture stated in the SDD. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of alert prioritisation/consolidation with basic alerts retained — individual alerts still presented but not prioritised or consolidated into a single ordered list
fha.effAc: Alerts continue to be generated but are no longer consolidated or prioritised; during a multiple-failure or high-alert-rate condition the crew must sort competing alerts unaided, delaying identification of the most critical condition and its procedure.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to triage un-prioritised alerts, most significant during a busy phase or a cascade of alerts; risk of attending the wrong condition first.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Basic alerting retained so no failure is fully missed, but loss of prioritisation/consolidation produces a significant increase in crew workload during multi-failure scenarios; proposed Major for confirmation. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Spurious fire/overheat warning presented with no actual fire or overheat
fha.effAc: Unnecessary crew response to a false warning (e.g. engine shutdown, extinguisher discharge, diversion) reduces available thrust/redundancy against a nuisance cause.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload and distraction responding to a false fire indication; potential unnecessary engine shutdown / diversion decision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants affected other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect ranges from a nuisance alert (crew confirms no corroborating indication) to an unnecessary engine shutdown/diversion depending on crew procedure and corroboration available; the function definition alone does not fix which outcome governs, so severity is left for engineering judgement on the assumed crew response and any cross-check with overheat/parameter data. Left empty rather than reaching for Minor.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to detect an actual fire or overheat in a monitored zone (missed detection)
fha.effAc: An actual engine-nacelle or APU-compartment fire is not annunciated, so crew-commanded extinguishing is not initiated; fire in a fire zone can propagate to adjacent structure, fuel and systems unchecked.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no fire warning and take no fire-response action; first awareness may be secondary effects (thrust loss, smoke, systems degradation) at a later, less controllable stage.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Missed detection in an engine/APU fire zone denies the crew the means to command extinguishing before propagation; per the SDD extinguishing is a crew action gated on detection. Proposed Hazardous (large reduction in safety margins with an undetected fire in a high-energy/flammable fire zone). CONFIRM: if an undetected nacelle fire is shown non-survivable in some phases this is Catastrophic — that determination requires PRA/structural analysis, not the function definition. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of hold smoke detection at one or more stations
fha.effAc: Smoke detection coverage of the hold is reduced without annunciation; a hold fire in an affected station would not be detected, and the hold carries no suppression.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of reduced hold detection coverage; no crew action taken; first indication of a hold fire would come only if remaining stations detect it.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect turns on the consequence of an undetected hold fire with no suppression fitted — a decision the SDD records as an assumption to be substantiated. Whether reduced/absent hold detection is a safety-margin reduction and of what magnitude cannot be derived from the function definition and depends on the hold fire threat and the no-suppression substantiation. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of fire/overheat detection in one monitored zone
fha.effAc: Detection is lost for one zone (a single engine nacelle, APU compartment, bleed duct run or gear bay); a fire/overheat in that specific zone would not be annunciated, while detection in all other zones remains.
fha.effCrew: Loss of that zone's detection is annunciated; crew are aware coverage of one zone is lost and can apply increased vigilance / procedural limitation for that zone.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect depends on which single zone loses detection (an engine/APU fire zone versus an overheat-only run) and whether crew awareness plus dispatch limitation adequately compensates; the function definition does not isolate the governing zone, so the severity is left for engineering judgement on the worst-case zone. Not defaulted to Minor.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degradation to single-loop detection logic in a zone on loss of one detection loop
fha.effAc: Detection in the affected zone remains available but reverts from dual-loop AND logic to single-loop, reducing the resistance to a spurious warning and removing loop redundancy; detection capability itself is retained.
fha.effCrew: Loss of one loop is annunciated; crew aware the zone is on single-loop logic, with detection still functional.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Detection remains available on the surviving loop, so this is a redundancy/robustness degradation rather than a loss of the safety function; whether it is a slight reduction in safety margin depends on the resulting spurious-warning and undetected-second-loop-failure exposure, which the function definition does not quantify. Left empty rather than defaulting to Minor.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: complete loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: An actual fire or overheat in a monitored fire zone (engine nacelle, APU compartment, bleed duct run, main gear bay) is not annunciated; crew receive no warning to actuate the fire handle, so a fire in a fire zone can progress unaddressed toward uncontained damage to structure and adjacent systems.
fha.effCrew: No fire/overheat alert presented; crew continue normal duties unaware, and the means to arm/actuate extinguishing is not triggered by any indication.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect stated.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected fire in a fire zone removes the crew's opportunity to actuate extinguishing, a large reduction in safety margins. Not committed Catastrophic: the SDD provides no fire-progression or burn-through timeline to substantiate loss of the airplane; that determination is left to the engineer. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: inadvertent extinguishant discharge with no fire
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: An extinguisher bottle discharges into a nacelle with no fire present, consuming a first-shot resource; because the two bottles per engine pair are cross-plumbed, suppression capability to that pair is reduced but not eliminated. No aircraft damage from the discharge itself is stated.
fha.effCrew: Nuisance discharge status / fire-handle indication presented; crew assess and confirm no fire, a workload increase and a diversion of attention.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect stated.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reduced extinguishing reserve to the affected engine pair with cross-plumbing retained, plus a nuisance event, is a significant reduction in a functional capability. No stated effect on flight path or structure supports a higher class. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: failure to discharge on crew command
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: On a detected engine or APU fire the crew actuates the fire handle but no extinguishant reaches the affected zone; the fire is not suppressed by the intended means and can progress toward uncontained damage to structure and adjacent systems.
fha.effCrew: Crew have actioned the correct procedure but the fire is not extinguished; increased workload managing an unsuppressed fire and any diversion/emergency-descent decision.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect stated.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An unextinguished fire in a fire zone after correct crew action is a large reduction in safety margins. Not committed Catastrophic: no fire-progression/burn-through timeline is provided to substantiate loss of the airplane; the engineer determines whether cross-plumbed reserve to the pair alters this. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: failure to discharge on crew command undetected until demanded
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: A latent failure of the discharge path is not revealed until the crew actuates the fire handle on a detected fire; at that moment no extinguishant reaches the zone and the fire is not suppressed, progressing toward uncontained damage. The latency means no prior opportunity to detect and correct.
fha.effCrew: Crew action produces no extinguishing when required; increased workload managing an unsuppressed fire, with no earlier annunciation to prompt corrective action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect stated.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An unextinguished fire after correct crew action, with the failure latent until demanded, is a large reduction in safety margins. Not committed Catastrophic: no fire-progression timeline is provided; latency raises exposure but the FHA does not quantify it. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: loss of extinguishing to one engine zone
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Extinguishing cannot be delivered to one nacelle of an engine pair on a detected fire; because the pair is cross-plumbed the paired bottle still serves the other nacelle, but the affected zone has no first-shot suppression, allowing a fire there to progress unaddressed.
fha.effCrew: Crew actuation of the handle yields no suppression to the affected zone; increased workload managing an unsuppressed fire in that nacelle.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect stated.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of first-shot suppression to one fire zone on a detected fire is a large reduction in safety margins. Not committed Catastrophic: no fire-progression timeline is provided, and cross-plumbing preserves suppression to the paired nacelle; the residual to the affected zone is the engineer's judgement. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of APU fire extinguishing capability (partial loss of fire extinguishing capability)
fha.effAc: APU compartment fire cannot be extinguished by the fixed bottle; APU fire relies on automatic detection/shutdown/fuel isolation and, on the ground unattended, automatic discharge, which is lost. Engine extinguishing unaffected.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains fire handles for engine zones; for APU fire the crew is limited to APU shutdown and fuel isolation with no extinguishant available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a class from the SDD alone: the aircraft-level outcome of an unextinguished APU fire depends on APU compartment fire-zone containment, APU location relative to the pressure boundary/structure, and whether automatic shutdown+fuel isolation alone bounds the fire — none stated. Needs engineering judgement / PRA disposition before a class.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire extinguishing capability
fha.effAc: No means to extinguish or suppress fire in any engine nacelle or the APU compartment; an ignited engine or APU fire cannot be controlled and may propagate to structure, fuel or adjacent systems.
fha.effCrew: Fire handles provide detection/isolation (shutoff, fuel isolation) but discharge is unavailable; crew cannot extinguish a detected fire and must divert with an uncontrolled fire.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncontrollable in-flight engine or APU fire with no extinguishing means available, given the fuel and high-energy fire zones (nacelles, wing fuel tanks), can progress to loss of the airplane. Proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous cylinder pressure / status indication (crew aware)
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the aircraft; oxygen supply itself is unaffected — the fault is in the indication path only.
fha.effCrew: Displayed cylinder pressure / system status disagrees with the true state; where the error is apparent or cross-checked at the pre-flight pressure check (a dispatch item), the crew treats indication as suspect and may reject dispatch or manage conservatively.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous indication that the crew can recognise (aware case) drives a slight workload increase and a conservative dispatch/management decision; oxygen delivery is unaffected. Proposed for engineer confirmation. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous cylinder pressure / status indication reading normal (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: No direct effect on the aircraft; supply is degraded/depleted but indication masks it.
fha.effCrew: Status reads normal while true oxygen reserve is inadequate; the crew is not alerted and continues normal duties, then during a decompression, smoke or fume event finds insufficient oxygen for the descent and diversion — impairing crew task performance at the moment it is required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected loss of adequate crew oxygen reserve, revealed only during a depressurisation/smoke event when the oxygen is needed for descent and diversion, can produce crew physical distress/impairment coincident with an emergency (a second event). Proposed as Hazardous for engineer confirmation; classification depends on the assumed coincidence of the depressurisation/smoke event. [anchor HAZ-2 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew breathing oxygen supply
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect; the aircraft remains controllable, but the crew has no protection against a loss-of-pressurisation, smoke or fume event at or near the maximum operating altitude (FL260) and for the descent/diversion that follows.
fha.effCrew: Crew unprotected against hypoxia on depressurisation and against smoke/fumes; requires immediate emergency descent to a breathable altitude; incapacitation possible if a triggering event occurs before descent is completed.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects support a large reduction in safety margins for the depressurisation/smoke case at altitude with the crew reliant on emergency descent; classification is contingent on an emergency descent to a breathable altitude always being available within crew tolerance, which the SDD does not establish — confirm before committing. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen to one or more mask stations
fha.effAc: No direct aircraft effect; crew oxygen remains available to the unaffected mask stations via the two cylinders and crossover manifold, with regulators independent per mask.
fha.effCrew: Reduced number of protected crew stations; remaining crew retain oxygen and can conduct an emergency descent; increased workload to reconfigure and manage seating.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; no passenger effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effects support a significant reduction in redundancy of crew protection with the function still available to remaining masks; contingent on at least one mask station remaining supplied for each occupant required for the descent. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The four systems the SDD designates as resources (FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS) and the two structural items (nose-door load path, hold hard points) are correctly excluded from the aircraft function list.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any resource is intended as an aircraft function, additional top functions and their decompositions would be required.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS and nose-door/hold structure from all add_function actions.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.rationale: The prompt's modeling rule and the SDD both classify these as resources/structure, not functions; I relied on that to omit them.

assumptions.text: Pitch, roll, yaw and high-lift are sub-functions of a single aircraft-level 'Control aircraft trajectory' function rather than separate top-level functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If they belong at aircraft-function level, four separate top functions replace one, changing the AFHA row structure.

citations.quote: provides the control authority required across the flight envelope

assumptions.rationale: The SDD groups them under one flight-control purpose; the correct AFHA altitude for these is an engineering judgment call.

assumptions.text: Fire detection and fire extinguishing are separately-failable and warrant distinct sub-functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection and discharge share a dominant common cause, they should be one sub-function, altering the fire decomposition.
assumptions.usedFor: 'Detect fire and overheat' vs 'Extinguish engine and APU fire' sub-functions.

citations.quote: DC power from the essential bus to detection and from the hot battery bus to the discharge circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes distinct hardware and power sources (detection on essential bus, discharge on hot battery bus) but does not state they fail independently.

assumptions.text: For SF-003/004/005 the TL-with-two-partials modelling style is used (complete loss plus within-MAC and outside-MAC degraded partials) rather than TL = loss of minimum acceptable configuration.
assumptions.ifWrong: Partial-loss entries would collapse to a single degraded-mode phrase and the within/outside-MAC split would move to the FHA effects instead.
assumptions.rationale: The provided function list and SDD do not fix which TL modelling convention the programme has adopted for control axes.

assumptions.text: Slowly developing erroneous/uncommanded control-axis and thrust behaviour can progress below crew detection thresholds, justifying the crew-Unaware rows.
assumptions.ifWrong: The crew-Unaware rows for SF-003/004/005 and SF-001 would be removed and those conditions covered on the Aware rows only.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001 Unaware, SF-003 Unaware, SF-004 Unaware, SF-005 Unaware

citations.quote: Degraded laws are annunciated.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes annunciation of degraded laws and jam discretes but does not establish detection thresholds for slow-onset control errors, so the undetectable-variant assumption is unverified.

assumptions.text: Crew Indication/Annunciation and Mitigation fields are left empty for these functions because the SDD describes system-level annunciations (degraded-law, jam/asymmetry discretes) but no established aircraft-function-level detection or crew procedure tied to each failure condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: Indication and mitigation cells would be populated from the FCS/PRP operation sections rather than left amber for engineer fill.

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes; high-lift position to the performance computation

assumptions.rationale: Per the abstention rule, indication/mitigation cannot be grounded until effects and detection means are analysed against each specific failure condition.

assumptions.text: High-lift asymmetry and runaway are detected in flight via the asymmetry-brake trip and its annunciation, so the crew-Aware variant applies to the commanded/uncommanded-motion malfunctions.
assumptions.ifWrong: An erroneous/asymmetric high-lift condition that develops undetected would need its own crew-Unaware row and could raise the classification the AFHA later assigns.

citations.quote: through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes asymmetry brakes at each section but does not explicitly state a flight-deck annunciation, so the awareness tag for the SF-006 malfunction cell is inferred.

assumptions.text: Braking degradation and asymmetry are the sizing-margin concern on the semi-prepared strip, so partial-loss braking conditions are the safety-relevant ones the AFHA will weigh against the 1,080 m vs 1,800 m margin.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the margin does not absorb the degraded case, the partial-loss braking condition drives a different downstream classification and requirement set.

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m, and the margin between the two is the basis

assumptions.rationale: The SDD ties braking assessment to the landing-distance margin but does not quantify degraded-braking stopping distance, forcing a qualitative partial-loss phrasing.

assumptions.text: An erroneous nose-door lock-status indication (indicated-locked while truly unlocked) can develop below crew detection because it defeats one of the two dissimilar sensing paths, keeping a crew-Unaware variant on SF-010.
assumptions.ifWrong: If dual dissimilar sensing fully precludes a misleading indication, the SF-010 crew-Unaware erroneous-indication condition drops out.

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts dual dissimilar sensing but gives no coverage evidence that both paths cannot be simultaneously misleading, so an undetected erroneous-indication variant is retained.

assumptions.text: Ground flotation loss (footprint pressure exceeding what the operating surface accepts) is a distinct partial-loss condition of SF-007 separate from a rolling/support loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If flotation is not a separable failure condition, the SF-007 partials collapse and the combined SF-007+SF-008 flag is unnecessary.

citations.quote: to achieve the flotation the semi-prepared surface demands

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists flotation as a stated purpose but does not state a crew indication for exceeding surface bearing capacity, so the awareness/indication fields are left empty.

assumptions.text: The nose-door lock status displayed to the crew makes total and partial loss of locking capability crew-Aware, while a false-confirmation malfunction is inherently crew-Unaware.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-011 unaware malfunction row would fold into the Aware row and the false-confirmation condition would lose its dedicated undetected-case treatment.

citations.quote: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times and is included in the take-off configuration check.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the indication means but not the failure-detection coverage of the false-agreement case, forcing a split by awareness rather than a single row.

assumptions.text: Loss of strap tension at a single station and at two adjacent stations are distinct annunciated conditions, and sub-threshold loss can develop crew-Unaware.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-012 unaware row would be removed if all restraint loss is in fact annunciated at any magnitude.

citations.quote: loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a restraint condition requiring immediate attention

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states single-strap and two-adjacent-station annunciations exist but does not give the tension threshold below which loss goes undetected.

assumptions.text: The single instrumented tension loop can produce an erroneous adequate-tension indication that masks a real restraint loss, and this develops crew-Unaware.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-013 unaware false-OK malfunction row would be reclassified or removed if independent cross-checks preclude undetected masking.

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item.

assumptions.rationale: The loop is described as a single instrumented loop with coverage recorded as an open item, so its failure-to-detect mode is credible but unquantified in the SDD.

assumptions.text: Cabin pressure state is displayed via avionics so most pressurisation-control failures are crew-Aware, but a slow differential drift can fall below detection.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-015 unaware slow-drift malfunction row would be removed if a cabin-altitude alert reliably captures all drift rates.

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.rationale: The SDD confirms cabin altitude is displayed but gives no alert threshold or rate limit that would bound an undetected slow drift.

assumptions.text: The independent standby instrument provides an effective cross-check that renders misleading primary-display information crew-detectable in the aware case.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-018 misleading-information malfunction would migrate fully to the crew-Unaware row and the aware-row mitigation would not hold, changing downstream AFHA classification.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018 malfunctions[] awareness split and mitigation fields

citations.quote: a standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the standby shares nothing with the primaries but does not state crew procedure or detection thresholds, so detectability of misleading data is inferred.

assumptions.text: A missed alert or missed fire/overheat detection can develop below crew detection thresholds because no independent cue exists once the sensing channel fails silently.
assumptions.ifWrong: If failure monitoring annunciates loss of the alerting/detection channel itself, the missed-alert and missed-detection conditions become crew-Aware, collapsing the Unaware rows for SF-019 and SF-020.

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: The SDD grounds the annunciation paths but not the failure-annunciation (monitoring) coverage, so the undetected variants are retained on the Unaware row.

assumptions.text: Hold smoke detection loss at individual stations is not independently annunciated to the crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If station health is monitored the undetected hold-detection-loss condition becomes crew-Aware and moves off the SF-020 Unaware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020 crew-Unaware malfunctions[] entry for hold smoke detection

citations.quote: The hold has smoke detection at nine stations along its length and no suppression

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes nine detection stations but does not describe monitoring of the detection stations' own health.

assumptions.text: SF-021 extinguishing failure on command is not evident until the crew pulls a fire handle, so it carries a crew-Unaware row for the latent case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a discharge-readiness monitor exists, the SF-021 Unaware row collapses and that condition moves to the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021 Unaware row (failure to discharge on crew command)

citations.quote: Extinguishing in the engine and APU zones is a crew action through the fire handles

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states extinguishing is a crew action but does not describe continuous discharge-readiness monitoring, so the latent-failure detectability could not be confirmed.

assumptions.text: SF-022 oxygen supply degradation can develop below the continuous pressure indication resolution and thus keeps a crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If low-pressure alerting captures all credible degradation rates, the SF-022 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022 Unaware row (reduced reserve, erroneous indication reading normal)

citations.quote: cylinder pressure and system status to the flight deck; low pressure alerting

assumptions.rationale: The SDD confirms continuous pressure display and low-pressure alerting but not the threshold or leak-rate detectability, so a slow-developing undetected loss cannot be ruled out.

assumptions.text: SF-021 total loss of extinguishing is only a distinct failure condition in combination with a concurrent engine/APU fire (SF-020), which the engineer should record as a Combined condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If treated standalone, the extinguishing FC severity/context in the AFHA is understated versus the fire-present combined case.

citations.quote: two bottles per engine pair with cross-plumbing; independent APU protection

assumptions.rationale: Table A3 flags related sub-functions requiring combined conditions; the extinguishing function's consequence depends on the fire-detection function's state, which is a separate function outside this turn.

assumptions.text: The Aeolus HL-1 hold is unoccupied in flight, so 'passenger' effects reduce to flight-crew-only effects for all SF-001 malfunction rows.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA effect-on-occupants column needs an occupant model; the provided inputs state crew-only carriage, which I relied on for every effPax field.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold, effPax and potentially the severity of the asymmetry rows would change.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-001-M, SF-001-M2, SF-001-M3, SF-001-M4, SF-001-M5

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: An outboard-engine thrust asymmetry at the 28 m moment arm is the worst credible directional-control case for the aware SF-001-M3 condition, and the same-side second-engine case is the potential Catastrophic driver.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA needs a worst-credible-case to classify SF-001-M3; the SDD names the outboard-engine case as the directional-control sizing case and the same-side second-engine case as outside the design dispatch case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a worse credible asymmetry exists (or the sizing case is less severe), the proposed Hazardous class for SF-001-M3 changes.

citations.quote: Loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case and is retained as a condition to be studied.

assumptions.text: No project failure condition SF-001-M5 exists; the turn asked for a row I have no FCIM grounding for.
assumptions.rationale: The provided FCIM for SF-001 lists SF-001-M and SF-001-M4 only; SF-001-M2, M3 and M5 are not present as FCIM entries, forcing an ungrounded row for M5.
assumptions.ifWrong: If these conditions are added to the FCIM with bounded effects, the M2/M3/M5 rows can be re-derived and classified.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-M5 (and the missing-FCIM note on SF-001-M2, SF-001-M3)

assumptions.text: An uncommanded in-flight deployment of one inboard reverser produces an asymmetry that can lead to loss of control and loss of the airplane.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states reversers are inboard-only and details in-flight inhibits but does not state the controllability outcome if those inhibits are defeated in flight; the Catastrophic class for SF-002-M leans on this.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the inboard moment arm and rudder authority render an in-flight single-reverser deployment controllable across the envelope, SF-002-M would drop from Catastrophic to Hazardous or Major.

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only. Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight

assumptions.text: Complete loss of all four engines leaves no propulsive source and commits the aircraft to a forced landing normally resulting in loss of the airplane.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names four turbofans as the thrust source for all phases and no alternative propulsion; the Catastrophic class for SF-001-TL depends on there being no other thrust means.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an unstated alternative propulsion or glide-landing credit changes the outcome, SF-001-TL severity would change.

citations.quote: Four podded turbofans on pylons beneath the high wing provide thrust for all phases of flight

assumptions.text: The one-engine-out design case (survivable to a suitable aerodrome) bounds a partial thrust loss as a significant, not catastrophic, degradation.
assumptions.rationale: Needed to place SF-001-PL at Major; the SDD states the aircraft continues to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at/after V1.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a partial-loss case (e.g. two engines same side, outside the design dispatch case) is the intended interpretation, SF-001-PL could be Hazardous or Catastrophic.

citations.quote: designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.text: The flight deck is the only occupied compartment in flight; the hold carries payload only and is unoccupied.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA occupant-effect column needs to know who is exposed; the functions list alone does not state occupancy.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the hold could be occupied in flight, the Effect on Occupants column and possibly the severity of every pitch condition would change.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-002-TL, SF-003-M, SF-003-M2, SF-003-M3, SF-003-M4

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is a supplement to wheel braking, not the primary ground-deceleration means, so loss of reverse alone does not by itself determine the stopping outcome.
assumptions.rationale: Whether SF-002-TL has a stateable aircraft effect depends on whether reverse is on the critical stopping path; the function definition does not resolve this.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reverse thrust is on the critical stopping path on the semi-prepared surface, SF-002-TL would carry a stateable and potentially significant aircraft effect and severity rather than a blank.

citations.quote: Predicted landing rollout at maximum landing weight is approximately 1,080 m.

assumptions.text: An erroneous or uncommanded pitch response of sufficient magnitude at a critical flight phase can exceed available recovery authority and lead to loss of the airplane.
assumptions.rationale: The proposed Catastrophic class for SF-003-M and -M2 rests on the achievable magnitude/rate exceeding recovery capability, which the function list states qualitatively but not quantitatively.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the erroneous/uncommanded pitch is magnitude-bounded by design (limited authority/envelope protection) such that recovery is always available, SF-003-M and -M2 could drop to Hazardous or Major.

assumptions.text: The design payload is a single high-mass unitised blade with a narrow CG envelope such that an outside-MAC loss of pitch authority is a credible aircraft-level condition.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA distinguishes within-MAC and outside-MAC partial pitch loss but the SDD gives no CG envelope or stability-margin data to bound the outside-MAC case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If outside-MAC pitch loss is not credible or is bounded to recoverable margins, SF-003-PL2 severity drops from Hazardous toward Major or the row folds into SF-003-PL.

citations.quote: one wind-turbine blade of up to 105 m and 72.6 t, carried whole

assumptions.text: 'Complete loss of pitch control' means loss by every available means including the mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion path.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim, so 'complete loss' must be read as all paths lost or the condition would not be total.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the mechanical reversion path is retained under this condition, SF-003-TL is a partial-loss condition, not total, and severity would reduce from Catastrophic.

citations.quote: a survivable but degraded means of control with all three flight control computers lost

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so no passenger/occupant effects apply to any of these conditions.
assumptions.rationale: Effects on occupants must be stated; the SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight and crew are the only occupants.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants can be carried in the hold, occupant effects and potentially severity would change on the impaired-control conditions.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so no passenger-injury effect applies to any SF-004 condition.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA effect-on-occupants column requires knowing whether occupants are exposed; the function list does not state occupancy, so I relied on the SDD mission description.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any occupants are carried in the hold in flight, each row's effPax would need an occupant-injury effect and could raise TL/PL2 severity via HAZ-3/CAT-1 occupant criteria.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-004-TL, SF-004-PL, SF-004-PL2, SF-004-M3, SF-004-M4

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: Complete loss of the roll axis has no residual roll-control means (mechanical reversion covers stabiliser trim and lower rudder only, not roll).
assumptions.rationale: The Catastrophic classification of SF-004-TL depends on there being no survivable degraded roll path; the function list alone does not establish this, so I leaned on the SDD reversion description.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a residual roll-control means exists in the TL case, SF-004-TL would degrade below Catastrophic and its CAT-1 basis would not hold.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: The outboard-engine-out at V1 with maximum blade payload directional-control sizing case governs the severity of erroneous/partial yaw conditions near the ground.
assumptions.rationale: The AFHA severity for yaw conditions needs a worst-phase aircraft effect; the SDD names this as the sizing case but the FHA must confirm it drives the worst case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a different phase/case is worse, the Hazardous/Major proposals for SF-005-M, M2 and PL could shift up or down.

citations.quote: The sizing case for directional control is an outboard engine failure at V1 with the maximum blade payload

assumptions.text: The mechanical reversion path to the lower rudder segment provides a survivable recovery means that keeps erroneous/uncommanded yaw below Catastrophic.
assumptions.rationale: The distinction between Hazardous and Catastrophic for the aware yaw-malfunction conditions rests on whether a recovery means remains; the SDD asserts one but the FHA must confirm its authority is sufficient.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the reversion path cannot arrest an erroneous/uncommanded yaw, SF-005-M and SF-005-M2 could be Catastrophic.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so occupant effects are limited to the flight crew for all SF-005 conditions.
assumptions.rationale: The occupant-effect column depends on who is aboard; the SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried, the passenger-effect column and possibly the severities would change.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: The directional-control sizing case (outboard engine failure at V1 with maximum blade payload) is the worst-case asymmetry that yaw control must counter across the applicable flight phases.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA is implementation-agnostic but the only quantitative driver for yaw-control severity in the provided inputs is the SDD sizing statement; no separate handling-qualities data was supplied.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a more or less severe asymmetry governs, SF-005-TL and SF-005-PL2 proposed classes (Catastrophic / Hazardous) would move.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: The flight crew is the only occupant set exposed in flight (hold unoccupied), so passenger effects are not a severity driver for these conditions.

assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants can be carried in the hold, the passenger-effect fields and possibly the severities for the hold-related conditions would change.

assumptions.text: A fire in an engine nacelle or APU compartment that is neither detected nor extinguished can progress to uncontained damage of structure and adjacent systems within the flight.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names these as fire zones but provides no fire-progression, burn-through or time-to-consequence data, which is required to distinguish Hazardous from Catastrophic.
assumptions.ifWrong: If progression is slow enough to be managed by diversion/shutdown alone, SF-020-TL, SF-021-M2, -M3 and -PL could fall to Major; if fast enough to cause loss of the airplane, they could rise to Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: Severity of SF-020-TL, SF-021-M2, SF-021-M3, SF-021-PL

assumptions.text: Cross-plumbing preserves extinguishing to the unaffected nacelle of a pair, so SF-021-PL degrades one zone rather than an engine pair.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes cross-plumbing but the SFHA condition is scoped to 'one engine zone'; the boundary of the loss depends on where the failure sits in the plumbing.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single failure defeats extinguishing to both nacelles of a pair, SF-021-PL is understated and should be re-scoped as loss to an engine pair.
assumptions.usedFor: Effects and severity of SF-021-PL, SF-021-M

assumptions.text: An unextinguished engine fire (SF-021-TL) can propagate to fuel tanks/structure and is not bounded by nacelle fire-zone containment alone.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states nacelles are fire zones and fuel is present in the wing, but does not state whether containment alone bounds an unextinguished fire without discharge.
assumptions.ifWrong: If nacelle containment plus shutdown/fuel-isolation bounds the fire without discharge, SF-021-TL may drop below Catastrophic.

assumptions.text: The severity of SF-022-M3 assumes coincidence with a depressurisation or smoke/fume event that requires crew oxygen.
assumptions.rationale: Crew oxygen has no effect in normal flight; its aircraft-level consequence only arises when the oxygen is called upon.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the depletion is detected before the event (e.g. by the pre-flight check being effective against this fault), SF-022-M3 reduces below Hazardous.

assumptions.text: The APU compartment (SF-021-PL2) is a fire zone whose consequence on loss of extinguishing depends on containment and location not stated in the SDD.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD identifies the APU as a fire zone but gives no aircraft-level outcome for an unextinguished APU fire, forcing abstention on severity.
assumptions.ifWrong: If APU shutdown+fuel isolation plus containment bounds the fire, SF-021-PL2 could be classified lower; if it can breach structure/pressure boundary, higher.

assumptions.text: An emergency descent to a breathable altitude is always available within crew physiological tolerance following complete loss of crew oxygen at FL260.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the oxygen system's purpose covers the descent and diversion after a pressurisation/smoke event but does not establish that descent is always achievable within crew tolerance without oxygen.
assumptions.ifWrong: If descent is not reliably achievable in time, SF-022-TL rises toward Catastrophic (crew incapacitation / loss of the airplane) rather than Hazardous.

assumptions.text: The hold remains unoccupied in flight, so no failure condition of the crew oxygen function has any passenger/occupant effect.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA occupant-effect column requires an occupancy state; the SDD asserts no in-flight hold occupancy but this is a dispatch/operational assumption to confirm.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants are ever carried in the hold in flight, an occupant-oxygen effect would apply and could raise several rows.

assumptions.text: At least one mask station remains supplied for each crew member required to conduct the emergency descent in the SF-022-PL case.
assumptions.rationale: The proposed Major for partial loss depends on remaining protected stations; the SDD gives independent regulators per mask but does not bound how many stations a single failure removes.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a partial loss can leave a required crew station unprotected, SF-022-PL approaches the SF-022-TL classification.
